subject: AWS listing: clarify "Cost to Deploy" examples & tenant-isolation entitlements
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-retail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft AWS listing + a quick procurement question

Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — the demo helped. Attached is a consolidated request from our procurement team: they want clearer 'cost to implement' examples on the product page and explicit language around tenant isolation (we're a multi-tenant SaaS integrating with several retail backends). Two quick asks from procurement:

- Can the product page show 2–3 realistic implementation examples with rough OPEX/one-time estimates? (e.g., SSO integration, data ingestion, low-latency inference pipeline)
- We need a short, plain-language entitlement statement for the listing that says whether data is segregated and what safeguards are in place (KMS, VPC, audit logs).

I've attached their template and our internal notes. Can you share an updated marketplace copy with these explicit examples by EOD Thursday? Procurement also asked for a diagram they can include in their internal brief.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Integrations, Acme Retail

Folks — forwarding Acme's procurement asks. Key product page changes they want: explicit "Cost to Deploy" examples and a one-paragraph tenant isolation entitlements blurb.

Notes / constraints:
- Keep examples concrete but conservative (they'll show to finance). Use ballpark numbers and callouts for assumptions (e.g., 1 TB ingestion/month, 4 concurrent inference nodes).
- The entitlement blurb must map to our Private/Dedicated offerings: reference KMS, VPC peering, audit logs, and "per-tenant KV cache segregation" where applicable; but avoid implying guaranteed data residency beyond region.
- They asked for a diagram (attached). Marissa: can you draft the ENTITLEMENT copy + 2 short deployment examples? Kim: can you sanity-check the phrasing against Marketplace policy and the AMI/PrivateOffer constraints? Jonas: can you confirm whether the diagram matches how Dedicated would be configured?

Timeline: EOD Thursday (18th) is their internal deadline — realistically we should aim for Wednesday EOD to allow back-and-forth.

Thanks — Vivek

Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft AWS listing + a quick procurement question

Thanks — I sketched two implementation examples and a short entitlement paragraph below. Pasting copy that could slot into the AWS product page (concise bullets + one-liner for entitlements).

--- Suggested "Cost to Deploy" examples (short bullets for product page):
1) Quick-start (SMB pilot) — 1 week to integrate SSO + onboarding, estimated first-month OPEX ~$1,200 (managed inference credits + data transfer). Assumes single VPC peering and <200K tokens/day.
2) Regional pilot (mid-market) — 3–4 weeks incl. ETL + schema mapping, expected OPEX ~$5k–$8k/mo and one-time migration effort ~$12k. Assumes 1 TB/month ingestion and 4 inference nodes for 99th percentile latency targets.

--- Entitlement blurb (proposed):
Redwood Inference offers flexible deployment options to meet enterprise isolation needs. For AWS Marketplace listings, customers can choose Hosted (shared), Dedicated (isolated GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Data can be encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS and segregated via VPC controls and audit logging. For Dedicated and Private deployments, per-tenant KV cache and storage isolation are enforced; contact sales for a PrivateOffer that documents your specific tenancy and residency requirements.

Attachments: I updated the draft listing doc (aws_listing_draft_v3.docx) with inline edits and added the cost-to-deploy matrix (cost-to-deploy-matrix.xlsx). Jonas — I left a placeholder in the diagram where we should show Dedicated topology.

Next steps: Kim, can you: 1) tighten the entitlement blurb to ensure it doesn't read like an SLA, 2) validate Marketplace policy (AMIs/PrivateOffers) language, and 3) suggest a short headline for the product page that calls out "predictable inference economics"?

Marissa
Product Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft AWS listing + a quick procurement question

Love the practical examples — good work. A few edits and policy notes below (I also updated the doc with tracked changes):

1) Entitlement paragraph: tighten to avoid binding commitments. Replace "are enforced" with "are available as part of Dedicated and Private deployments". Add a sentence: "Customers should refer to the PrivateOffer or contract for specific tenancy and residency guarantees."

2) Cost examples: label all estimates with assumptions and a simple sentence: "Estimates are illustrative and exclude AWS networking egress charges; contact sales for a custom quote." Procurement likes round numbers; I've adjusted ranges to be slightly broader.

3) Marketplace constraints:
- AMI/PrivateOffer: we can call out "Dedicated" and "Private" but avoid implying cross-account access guarantees unless configured via PrivateOffer.
- Avoid commitments about backup retention periods or log storage durations in product page copy — point customers to the support/SLA page for operational details.

4) Diagram: Jonas — when you update the topology, please add a small note for "KMS: customer-managed recommended" and mark where audit logs are collected (CloudTrail / S3).

I'll send a version to Acme after we incorporate Jonas' diagram. Recommend we produce a one-page PDF diagram for procurement to attach to their brief.

Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace Operations, Redwood Inference
